steps: تخيل أنك ترسم لوحة فنية رائعة، أحياناً تحتاج لتزيين أجزاء صغيرة داخل الرسمة دون إضافة ألوان جديدة في ورقتك الأساسية، وهنا يأتي دور العناصر الوهمية في لغة سي إس إس لتساعدنا على تزيين أجزاء خفية.
نكتب العنصر الوهمي باستخدام نقطتين رأسيتين مضاعفتين هكذا (::) لكي نفهمه ونفرقه عن بقية الأوامر، فمثلاً لتلوين أول حرف من الفقرة نكتب p::first-letter مع تحديد اللون المطلوب.
تعمل هذه العناصر الوهمية بطريقة سحرية حيث تقرأ أجزاء محددة تلقائياً من المستند وكأنها عناصر حقيقية، دون الحاجة لتعديل ملف إتش تي إم إل الأصلي وزيادة عدد السطور فيه.
يمكننا أيضاً استخدام ::first-line لتغيير تنسيق السطر الأول وحده في الفقرة، فإذا كبرت الشاشة أو صغرت، سيتكيف السطر الأول بنفسه ويظل مميزاً وجميلاً.
القاعدة الذهبية هنا هي أن العنصر الوهمي يتبع دائماً العنصر الأصلي، ولا يمكن أن يعيش بمفرده، وكأنك تضع قبعة جميلة فوق رأس شخص ما.
نستخدم هذه المهارة في الحياة اليومية لتصميم مواقع ويب مذهلة تشبه الألعاب والتطبيقات الشهيرة، مثل وضع علامات مميزة قبل العناوين أو إضافة رموز تعبيرية مرحة.
ar.example: لنفترض أننا نريد تلوين الحرف الأول من فقرة النص بلون مميز لتبدو القصة جذابة. نكتب في الكود: p::first-letter { color: #ff4757; font-size: 2em; }، وعند تشغيل الصفحة، سيقوم المتصفح تلقائياً بالتعرف على الحرف الأول وتكبيره وتلوينه باللون الأحمر المشرق.
ar.mistake: الخطأ الشائع هو استخدام نقطة واحدة مفردة هكذا (:first-letter) بدلاً من النقطتين (::). التصحيح هو دائماً استخدام نقطتين رأسيتين مضاعفتين للعناصر الوهمية في سي إس إس.
ar.recap: العناصر الوهمية تتيح لنا تزيين أجزاء محددة من العناصر بسهولة. وهي تستخدم نقطتين رأسيتين مضاعفتين لتحديد أجزاء مثل الحروف الأولى والأسطر بدقة.

steps: Imagine you are painting a wonderful artwork and need to decorate small parts without altering your main drawing. CSS pseudo-elements help us style these hidden or specific parts easily.
We write a pseudo-element using a double colon (::) to distinguish it from regular commands. For example, to color the first letter of a paragraph, we write p::first-letter.
These pseudo-elements work like magic, automatically targeting specific parts of the document as if they were real elements, without changing your original HTML file structure.
We can also use ::first-line to style only the first line of a paragraph. Whether the screen grows or shrinks, the first line automatically adapts and stays uniquely beautiful.
The golden rule here is that a pseudo-element always follows an originating element and cannot exist by itself, just like putting a cute hat on top of someone's head.
We use this skill in real life to design amazing web pages resembling famous games and apps, such as adding special marks before headings or cheerful emojis.
en.example: Suppose we want to color the first letter of a text paragraph to make the story engaging. We write in code: p::first-letter { color: #ff4757; font-size: 2em; }. When the page loads, the browser automatically detects the first letter and enlarges it with a bright red color.
en.mistake: A common mistake is using a single colon (:first-letter) instead of the double colon (::). The fix is to always use a double colon for pseudo-elements in CSS.
en.recap: Pseudo-elements let us style specific parts of elements easily. They use a double colon to precisely target elements like first letters and lines.

sections.text: Imagine you have a toy box and want to decorate just its corner without changing the whole box. CSS pseudo-elements do exactly this for web files. They let us choose a precise part of text, like the first letter or line, and style it uniquely.
sections.code: Welcome to the fun world of coding!
sections.output: The page displays with a large purple letter M.

sections.text: In classic children's storybooks, the first letter on a page is huge and colorful to catch young readers' attention. Using the ::first-letter pseudo-element, you can do this in any text paragraph on your website without extra HTML.
sections.code: Learning makes our minds smarter and stronger every single day.
sections.output: The first letter appears large and in a lovely pink color.

sections.text: Have you noticed how some books begin with special styled lines? The ::first-line pseudo-element helps you target the entire first line of a paragraph. No matter the screen size, the first line automatically adapts and highlights smartly.
sections.code: This is the first line and it will be a nice green color. The second line will stay completely normal.
sections.output: Only the first line appears in a dark green color.

sections.text: Imagine standing in a school line, and someone steps right at the very front. The ::before pseudo-element works this way, adding new content at the beginning of the selected element, like placing a badge or decorative stars before text.
sections.code: Lesson Two
sections.output: A shiny golden star appears right before the lesson heading.

sections.text: Just like friends sign their names at the end of notes, the ::after pseudo-element lets you place content at the very end of your target element. Today we will use it to place a cheerful emoji after every paragraph to make the site lively.
sections.code: I love designing web pages
sections.output: A friendly smiley face appears at the end of the paragraph text.

sections.h: The Importance of the content Property
sections.text: When you use ::before or ::after, the content property is the magic wand that makes the magic happen. Without this property inside your code, no text or symbol will appear, because it defines precisely what gets added to the browser.
sections.code: This is very important
sections.output: The phrase [Alert]: appears in red before the sentence.

sections.text: Have you noticed when you drag your computer mouse to select text, how its color changes? You can control this highlight color using the ::selection pseudo-element to keep your site coordinated with your favorite colors during user interaction.
sections.code: Drag your mouse over this text to see the magic!
sections.output: The highlighted text background turns into vibrant orange.

sections.text: In modern CSS, we use a double colon (::) for pseudo-elements to separate them from regular properties or classes. Always remember that a pseudo-element never stands alone; it always attaches to an originating element on the page.
sections.code: This text box contains special styled letters.
sections.output: The first letter of the div appears in a large clear blue font.
